concepts.name: PPP Model: Core Definition and Distinguishing Features
key_dimensions: Distinction between PPP and pure privatisation — government retains ownership/regulatory role
Distinction between PPP and traditional public procurement — risk transfer and private finance
Three essential elements: private investment, risk sharing, public service obligation
UPSC trap: PPP ≠ privatisation; why PPP still serves public purpose

concepts.name: Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) Model: Structure and Variants
key_dimensions: Concession period logic: private entity recoups investment through user charges, then transfers asset
Variants: BOT (Toll) vs BOT (Annuity) — who bears demand/traffic risk in each
Asset ownership during concession period vs after transfer — UPSC trap on 'ownership'
Sectors where BOT is dominant: highways (NHAI), ports — real examples

concepts.name: BOT Annuity vs BOT Toll: Risk Allocation Comparison
key_dimensions: In BOT Toll: revenue risk borne by private partner (user fee collection uncertainty)
In BOT Annuity: government pays fixed periodic payments — government bears demand risk
Why Annuity preferred for low-traffic corridors — viability argument
UPSC trap: confusing which party bears risk in each variant

concepts.name: Build-Own-Operate-Transfer (BOOT) vs BOT: Ownership Distinction
key_dimensions: BOOT: private entity owns asset during concession, unlike BOT where ownership may rest with government
Implications for balance sheet treatment and financing
Transfer obligation at end of concession — condition of asset at transfer
UPSC trap: 'own' in BOOT vs BOT — subtle but examinable ownership distinction

concepts.name: Design-Build-Finance-Operate (DBFO) Model
key_dimensions: Private partner responsible for all four stages — maximum private involvement short of full privatisation
Government's role limited to regulation and performance monitoring
Difference from BOT: design responsibility also transferred — affects innovation incentive
Used in UK's Private Finance Initiative (PFI) — international comparison angle

concepts.name: Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Contract: Characteristics
key_dimensions: Government retains ownership and capital investment; private party only manages operations
Minimum private risk compared to other PPP types — UPSC trap on calling it 'PPP'
Examples: urban water supply management, toll road operations handed to private operators
Difference from concession: no revenue rights necessarily transferred to private party

concepts.name: Management Contract vs Concession Contract: Key Differences
key_dimensions: Management contract: fee-based, private entity manages but does not bear commercial risk
Concession contract: private entity bears commercial/revenue risk over concession period
Asset ownership: remains with government in both, but risk profile differs sharply
UPSC trap: both involve private management — but risk transfer is the differentiator

concepts.name: Lease-Develop-Operate (LDO) / Rehabilitate-Operate-Transfer (ROT) Model
key_dimensions: Used for existing underperforming assets — private party leases, upgrades, operates
ROT variant: rehabilitation of brownfield infrastructure before operations
Distinguishing from greenfield BOT — existing asset vs new asset creation
Airport and port sector examples: AAI brownfield airport monetisation

concepts.name: Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM): Structure and Rationale
key_dimensions: Government pays 40% of project cost during construction; private party arranges 60%
Revenue risk shared: private party gets fixed annuity payments — not dependent on traffic
Introduced in 2016 for NHAI highway projects — context of stalled BOT projects
UPSC trap: HAM vs BOT Annuity — in HAM government also contributes upfront capital unlike pure annuity

concepts.name: Engineering-Procurement-Construction (EPC) Model vs PPP Models
key_dimensions: EPC: fully government-funded, private party is only a contractor — NOT a PPP model
No risk transfer to private party in EPC — government bears all commercial risk
UPSC trap: EPC often listed alongside PPP models in infrastructure policy — but it is not PPP
When government prefers EPC over PPP: low traffic, strategic/remote areas

concepts.name: Viability Gap Funding (VGF) in PPP Projects
key_dimensions: VGF bridges gap between project cost and commercially viable returns — makes unviable projects viable
Maximum VGF: 20% of project cost from Centre + additional 20% from state/sponsoring entity
UPSC trap: VGF does not mean project becomes fully public — private partner still operates and bears risk
Sectors covered under VGF scheme and 2021 expansion to social infrastructure (hospitals, schools)

concepts.name: Risk Allocation Framework in PPP Models
key_dimensions: Five major risk types: construction risk, demand/revenue risk, financial risk, regulatory risk, force majeure
Principle: risk should be borne by party best able to manage it
Comparison table: which risks are borne by government vs private in BOT, HAM, Annuity, EPC
UPSC trap: assuming private party always bears all risk in PPP — government often retains regulatory and force majeure risk

concepts.name: Concession Agreement: Key Elements and Enforceability
key_dimensions: Concession agreement as the legal backbone of PPP — defines rights, obligations, dispute resolution
Renegotiation problem: frequent renegotiation distorts original risk allocation
Termination clauses: compensation to private party if government terminates vs private party defaults
UPSC trap: concession ≠ license; concession grants operational rights over public asset for defined period

concepts.name: Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) in PPP Financing
key_dimensions: SPV created as a separate legal entity to ring-fence project risk from parent company
Enables non-recourse or limited-recourse project financing
UPSC trap: SPV is a financing/legal structure, not a PPP type itself — often confused
Government equity participation in SPV: changes pure PPP to joint venture — blurring classification

concepts.name: Public-Private-Partnership vs Joint Venture (JV): Conceptual Boundary
key_dimensions: JV: both parties hold equity and share profits/losses proportionally
PPP: government typically does not hold equity but sets regulatory framework and may provide VGF
Examples of JV in infrastructure: DIAL (Delhi International Airport Ltd) — government retains equity stake
UPSC trap: when government holds equity in SPV, it resembles JV — where does PPP end and JV begin?

concepts.name: PPP in Social Sector Infrastructure: Schools, Hospitals, Urban Services
key_dimensions: Challenges: difficulty in user-fee recovery in social sectors — hence more annuity/O&M models
Output-based aid and performance-linked payments as government tools
2021 VGF expansion to social infrastructure — significance and limitations
UPSC trap: assuming PPP is only for physical infrastructure like roads/ports — social sector PPP is equally relevant

concepts.name: Kelkar Committee Recommendations on PPP Reforms (2015)
key_dimensions: Key problem identified: one-sided contracts favouring government, no independent regulator
Recommendations: 3P India institution, infrastructure PPP Adjudication Tribunal, balanced risk sharing
Recommendation on renegotiation: structured process to prevent ad hoc changes
UPSC trap: Kelkar Committee on PPP ≠ Kelkar Committee on fiscal consolidation — two different committees

concepts.name: National Monetisation Pipeline (NMP) and PPP Linkage
key_dimensions: NMP: monetising brownfield government assets via PPP-type structures — InvIT, TOT, OM concession
Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT) model: government transfers toll collection rights for lump sum upfront — NHAI
Distinction: NMP is asset monetisation, not new asset creation — government retains ownership
UPSC trap: NMP ≠ privatisation; assets return to government after concession period

concepts.name: Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT) Model: Specific Features
key_dimensions: Private operator pays upfront concession fee to NHAI for right to collect tolls on existing highways
No construction risk for private party — pure revenue/demand risk
Difference from BOT Toll: in TOT, asset already exists and private party paid upfront; in BOT, private party builds
UPSC trap: TOT is a form of monetisation, not new investment — confusing it with fresh PPP for capacity creation

concepts.name: PPP Appraisal and Institutional Framework in India
key_dimensions: PPP Appraisal Committee (PPPAC) under DEA: approves central sector PPP projects above threshold
Role of Planning Commission's PPP Cell (now NITI Aayog) in model concession agreements
Model Concession Agreements (MCAs): standardised templates for highways, ports, airports — reduces transaction cost
UPSC trap: PPPAC approves PPP projects, not Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) for all — threshold matters
